accepted_interpretation.interpretation: The span defines f(x) = exp(gamma) log theta(x) product_{q <= x}(1-1/q) and claims that RH follows if exp(2/sqrt(x)) >= f(x) for every sufficiently large x. Its proof mechanism is contrapositive: under false RH, a cited Omega-plus premise is expanded into arbitrarily late positive lower-bound witnesses for log f, which eventually exceed 2/sqrt(x); taking logarithms of the proposed envelope instead imposes log f(x) <= 2/sqrt(x) at every sufficiently large input. These quantifiers are incompatible. Packaging the factors into f and moving to logarithms puts the pointwise ceiling and positive spikes on one additive scale, but the lemma remains only sufficient: it does not establish the envelope and depends on the cited Omega-plus result. The OCR-damaged exponent and threshold are not normalized here.

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: The span defines Psi(n) = n product_{q | n}(1+1/q), the primorial-type cutoff M_x = product_{q <= x} q, and R(n) = Psi(n)/(n log log n) for n >= 3, then states unconditionally that R(M_x) tends to exp(gamma)/zeta(2). Since M_x is squarefree and has exactly the primes q <= x as divisors, Psi(M_x)/M_x = product_{q <= x}(1+1/q), so substitution into R turns the cutoff-prime representation into a normalized quantity with a stable displayed limit. The normalization removes the explicit n factor and scales the remaining product by log log n. The limit gives neither a convergence rate nor the side of approach, so it cannot alone justify an eventual one-sided inequality when combined with another vanishing error.
